blocks.c: I did a normal shift. Three of them, actually.
It was the worst week of my life and nothing happened in it at all.
Tuesday: door closer on 22, still dying. Leak under the sink on 9. Fire panel showed a fault on zone 6 which cleared itself, which panels do, which is why they are all liars.

Wednesday: north stair smell. I finally found it, incidentally: a dead pigeon in the plenum above the 17th landing, which explained the spring and which is, in an entirely non-supernatural building, the worst part of my job.
Thursday: nothing. Genuinely nothing. Thirty-one landings, four times, and the only thing in my log is a note that the lobby ficus is dying again.
And through all of it, I could feel the building being polite to me.

That is the only way I can say it. Fourteen months of noises and complaints, and that week it was quiet. The chiller did not howl. The 22 door closer did not slam. On Thursday at 04:00 the freight car came down to B2 and opened its doors before I pressed anything, and sat there, waiting, with the light on.
I wrote that in the log: 04:02 — freight car self-called to B2, doors held open 40s, no call registered on the controller. I checked the controller. There was no call registered.
Then I wrote, underneath, because I could not help it:
And in the morning, when I opened the book to sign off, somebody had written under that. Not Wen's block capitals. Something else. Small, neat, old-fashioned, the handwriting of a clerk:
Of course. Friday. We are so looking forward to it.
Do bring the 1994 volume. We have been missing it.
